# gpsd

[gpsd.io](https://gpsd.io) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/gpsd](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/gpsd)

**Status: available.** 5 of OSS-Fuzz's 5 fuzz targets have statements. 20 binaries, 17 MB. 75 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 18 blocked by the model, 57 open.

Built from gpsd (commit `46977faa`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [FuzzClient](FuzzClient/) | NUL-terminates the input, then json_watch_read (?WATCH), json_device_read (?DEVICE) and, if a device path was parsed, parse_uri_dest; all return values discarded. | none | 15 |
| [FuzzDrivers](FuzzDrivers/) | Writes input[2:] to a non-blocking pipe and calls production gpsd_poll() up to 100 times (driver auto-detection then driver-specific packet parsing); input bytes 0/1 set readonly/passive; the change masks only steer the loop. | none | 15, 9 blocked by the model |
| [FuzzDriversStructured](FuzzDriversStructured/) | Byte 0 selects one of 10 GNSS protocols (SiRF, UBX, Zodiac, GeoStar, Navcom, NMEA, RTCM3, TSIP, GREIS, Skytraq); the harness frames the rest as a packet with a VALID checksum/CRC so it passes the lexer, writes it to a pipe and runs gpsd_poll() up to 100 times. The checksums are generated, not checked; nothing about the decoded state is asserted. | none | 15, 9 blocked by the model |
| [FuzzJson](FuzzJson/) | Replaces the first byte with '{', NUL-terminates, then libgps_json_unpack and json_toff_read into a zeroed gps_data_t; the second call's status is RETURNED to libFuzzer (a return code only, not a check). | none | 15 |
| [FuzzPacket](FuzzPacket/) | Loads the input into a gps_lexer_t and runs packet_parse, then (fresh lexer) packet_get on /dev/null until it returns <= 0; results discarded. | none | 15 |

## What the statements say, for gpsd
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch gpsd
    ./oft verify-sha gpsd

By hand: download `gpsd-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/gpsd/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [gitlab.com/gpsd/gpsd](https://gitlab.com/gpsd/gpsd) at `46977faa8f94eb036ca68c24a3fc0d233732e707`, built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `FuzzClient`, `FuzzDrivers`, `FuzzDriversStructured`, `FuzzJson` and `FuzzPacket` (see each harness page)
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.

## Licence
gpsd is under `BSD-2-Clause`. Each binary is a combined work of gpsd, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.10.0-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0-src): `gpsd-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `gpsd-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and `recipe.tar.zst`, that release's build recipe (the build scripts, pins and patches).
